entities.blurb: Lingering potions are variants of splash potions that can be thrown to leave clouds with status effects that linger on the ground in an area.
entities.name: Area Effect Cloud

entities.blurb: Display entities are entities useful for map or data pack creators to display various things. There are Block Displays, Item Displays and Text Displays, which are used to display blocks, items and texts respectively. They can be created only with the /summon or /execute summon command.
entities.name: Block Display

entities.blurb:
A wind charge is a throwable item made from breeze rods. It bursts into wind on impact, which can knock entities into the air and interact with doors, buttons, levers, and similar blocks. 
Breezes use special high-blast-radius wind charges as their ranged attack, which cannot be obtained by players.
entities.name: Wind Charge

entities.blurb: A cushion is a placeable entity that can be sat on. Cushions can be placed on any surface within any block in the game, excluding fluids and a few invisible blocks, and break shortly after their supporting block is removed.
entities.name: Cushion

entities.blurb:
The ender dragon is a giant flying hostile boss mob found when first entering the End. It is the largest naturally spawning mob in the game. Its attacks involve charging at the player and shooting fireballs that create damaging effect clouds. The ender dragon can be re-summoned by placing four End crystals around the exit portal.
Defeating the ender dragon the first time activates the exit portal which allows safe return to the Overworld. Each time it is defeated, an End gateway is created on the outskirts of the central island which can be used to teleport to the outer End islands.
entities.name: Dragon Fireball

labels: {{Animate|Dragon Fireball JE2.png; Dragon Fireball BE.png|16px}} Dragon fireball

entities.blurb: An egg is an item that is dropped by chickens every few minutes while they are still alive. It can be used to craft food items, such as cake, and can be thrown for a chance to spawn baby chickens on impact. They have three variants based on the variant of the corresponding chicken: the standard egg for temperate chickens, brown egg for warm chickens, and blue egg for cold chickens.
entities.name: Thrown Egg

entities.blurb: An ender pearl is an item that can be thrown to teleport to where it lands, or used to craft eyes of ender, which are required to access the End.
entities.name: Thrown Ender Pearl

entities.blurb: A bottle o' enchanting is an item that can be thrown to break it and release experience orbs.
entities.name: Thrown Bottle o' Enchanting

entities.blurb:
TNT is an explosive block that can be lit by a redstone signal, flint and steel, stray fire, flaming projectile or explosion.
When lit, TNT becomes primed TNT, a gravity-affected entity that produces a damaging, block-destroying explosion, usually after four seconds. Blocks destroyed by TNT always drop their usual items as if mined by a player.
entities.name: Primed TNT

entities.blurb: An evoker is a spell-casting illager that can be found in woodland mansions and as part of raids. They are the only source of totems of undying. Evokers use two spells to attack; one that summons armor-piercing fangs and one that summons vexes. This is the only way for vexes to spawn (without using Creative mode or commands).
entities.name: Evoker Fangs

entities.blurb:
Experience (EXP or XP for short) can be gained from defeating mobs or performing many kinds of other actions. Experience has no direct effect on the player character, but it can be used to enhance their equipment through enchanting, or by using an anvil to repair, rename, or combine enchantments on equipment. Most sources of experience are produced in the form of experience orbs. In Java Edition, experience gained affects the player's score on the death screen.
Experience orbs also recover durability on items with Mending that are being worn or are in-hand.
entities.name: Experience Orb

entities.blurb: An eye of ender is a craftable item that can be thrown in the Overworld to show the direction of the nearest stronghold, which may break the eye. 12 eyes of ender are required to activate a stronghold's End portal (which may generate with some of the eyes already in place), which leads to the End dimension.
entities.name: Eye of Ender

entities.blurb: A falling block is the entity form of a block that appears when a gravity-affected block loses its support.
entities.name: Falling Block

entities.blurb: A projectile is an entity that can be fired, shot, or thrown by mobs, other entities, dispensers, and players. Projectiles can also be summoned using /summon.
entities.name: Fireball

entities.blurb: A fishing rod is a tool that casts a bobber used to fish in water or to hook and pull mobs, items,‌[JE  only] and some other entities toward the player.
entities.name: Fishing Bobber

entities.blurb:
Interaction entities are a technical entity, useful for map or data pack creators to see who the last player to click on a certain spot is. They can only be created with the /summon or /execute summon commands.
Interaction entities are invisible, invincible and of a custom size. Their bounding box can be viewed via the F3 + B debug shortcut.
entities.name: Interaction

entities.blurb: Items are "dropped" blocks or items (non-block resources) that appear in the world, rather than being in the inventory of a player or block entity; they are a type of entity.
entities.name: Item

entities.blurb: Display entities are entities useful for map or data pack creators to display various things. There are Block Displays, Item Displays and Text Displays, which are used to display blocks, items and texts respectively. They can be created only with the /summon or /execute summon command.
entities.name: Item Display

entities.blurb: Leads are utility items used to leash and lead certain entities. Leashed entities can be tied to fences or other entities by using the fence or entity while sneaking. A lead can be removed from an entity by shearing it.
entities.name: Leash Knot

entities.blurb: A thunderstorm is an uncommon weather condition where lightning strikes occur and the sky becomes dark enough for monsters to spawn and players to sleep through the thunderstorm at any time of day.
entities.name: Lightning Bolt

entities.blurb: Llama spit is a projectile produced by llamas and trader llamas that deals a small amount of damage.
entities.name: Llama Spit

entities.blurb: Markers are entities intended for use in data packs and map-making. They can only be created with the /summon command.
entities.name: Marker

entities.blurb: Ominous item spawners are entities spawned by ominous trial spawners that display an item for 3 to 6 seconds before dispensing it downwards.
entities.name: Ominous Item Spawner

entities.blurb: The player is a unique entity or mob‌[BE  only] whose actions are controlled by a real person, and not the game itself. They are the main character of singleplayer Minecraft worlds, where most interactions and mechanics revolve around them as part of the gameplay. Players may also partake in the multiplayer mode with other players, putting more emphasis on player-driven activities.
entities.name: Player

entities.blurb: A projectile is an entity that can be fired, shot, or thrown by mobs, other entities, dispensers, and players. Projectiles can also be summoned using /summon.
entities.name: Shulker Bullet

entities.blurb: A small fireball is a fire charge launched as a projectile that deals burning damage and can start fires. They are used by blazes as their ranged attack, and cannot be thrown by hand.
entities.name: Small Fireball

entities.blurb: The minecart with monster spawner is a combination of a minecart and a monster spawner.
entities.name: Minecart with Monster Spawner

entities.blurb: Display entities are entities useful for map or data pack creators to display various things. There are Block Displays, Item Displays and Text Displays, which are used to display blocks, items and texts respectively. They can be created only with the /summon or /execute summon command.
entities.name: Text Display
